_readme: Machine-readable catalog of the PRODUCT component library (mirror of components/marketing/catalog.json for the authenticated app). The PreToolUse product-screen-guard injects a digest of this file into every write/edit under app/(dashboard)/** or components/product/**, so the full expressive range is in context on every generation, not just the primitives the model happens to remember. Two kinds of entry: `components` are shared components that already exist in this repo (import them), and `template` are shapes described here but NOT packaged yet (build them to the description instead of inventing a new shape). Keep entries in sync when props change; guard lines render as `Name(props) — use`.
contract: NEVER invent a component. The catalog below is the first stop for any container, tile, card, badge, meter or chart, and it is checked BEFORE markup is written, not after. If nothing here fits, build the new component in the existing visual language (tokens, radii, TILE_TONE tints, band height, type scale) and add it to this file in the same commit. Improvising a `<Box>` with a border and a radius is a defect even when it looks acceptable: it type-checks, it passes review, and it quietly grows a second design language. `product-lint` blocks the interactive form of this.

Before rendering a value, ask which catalog entry is the right shape for it. A counter set, a ratio, a share and a series each have a component — a run-on sentence of numbers is a defect, not a style.

Never invent a chart to fill space. A visual earns its place only when it answers a question the user actually asks, and only on data the payload already carries. Vanity metrics and decorative charts are forbidden (.claude/rules/app-ux.md).
Never hand-roll a shape that exists here. If the nearest entry does not fit, extend it (a prop, a mode) or build the `template` shape it describes, rather than writing a one-off.
Red is reserved for risk and failure. Commercial ceilings, queues and declines use `attention` (accent-3) — see usage-meter for the precedent.
Type scale: body1 14px, body2 12px, subtitle2 14px semibold, h5 18px, h4 20px. `caption` is below 12px — never for informative text.

tones.rule: Icon containers use TILE_TONE (bg-{tone}-light/10 + text-{tone}), tones primary | secondary | accent-1..4. Bars and meters use the UsageMeter vocabulary: primary | secondary | attention | empty. Status labels use the pastel badge, never colour alone.

components.name: EmptyState
components.props: icon, illustration? (an @/icons/illustrations/* element), title, badge?, description?, action?, secondaryAction?, className?, titleAs?, layout? (stack | row), framed?
components.use: Every zero-data view: icon + why it is empty + the ONE next action. Never a bare 'no data'. An area whose content is still being made passes badge (the translated "Em breve"), which renders as a StatusChip above the title. Inside a card whose title is the h2, pass titleAs="h3". A section or list with nothing in it is never left as empty space (the owner, 2026-11-09): give it an `illustration` (the template's line drawings in @/icons/illustrations, in the secondary hue), `layout="row"` for a short band (a section across the page, a table's empty overlay) and `framed={false}` inside a card. Pick the drawing by the subject, one per region of a screen: launch for the first item (the catalog, the roadmap, a first version), documentation for papers, records and a search with no result, platforms for machines, meetings and video, email for news and messages, experiment for recipes, accounts for people, access for rights and sign-ins, storage for backups, analytics for numbers and prices, configure for "nothing to do". A state of permission (a guide closed to the plan), of a record that does not exist or of a read that failed keeps its icon.

components.name: PageHeader
components.props: title, crumbs[{label,href?}], description? (behind the i), detail? (a line of state or data), chip?, action?
components.use: The title block of every member screen: the page's ONE <h1>, breadcrumbs back to the home, at most one action. What the screen is for goes behind the "i" beside the title (`description`, 200 characters at most, kept by lib/i18n/hint-budget.test.ts), never a paragraph read on every visit (the owner, 2026-11-09); `detail` is one line in sight only for state or data that tells the page apart (what an app does, what a meeting is about); `chip` says where the page's subject stands beside its title. Never hand-write an h1 + Breadcrumbs pair again.

components.name: SectionTitle
components.props: id, title, description? (behind the i), chip?, action?, as? (h2 | h3 | h4), variant? (h5 | h6 | subtitle1 | subtitle2: subtitle2 with as h3 for a section inside a card)
components.use: The heading of a section of a page that is not a card (a row of tiles, a group of cards, a table): its title, what it is behind the "i" beside it, where it stands (a StatusChip) and its own action at the right. Never an h2 with a paragraph under it (the owner, 2026-11-09). `variant` keeps the heading style of the screen's other sections (the member home's subtitle1, the catalog's h5). A card's head is CardTitle (template); until it is packaged, a card puts an InfoHint beside its own title.

components.name: UsageMeter
components.props: headline, caption?, segments[{key,label,value,display,tone}], ariaLabel
components.use: A consumption readout — used vs remaining, with each pool NAMED. Use for any x-of-y allowance (minutes, quota). Beats a plain progress bar when the pools differ in nature (cycle vs purchased).

components.name: MetricBars
components.props: items[{key,label,value,tone?,hint?,action?}], total?, spacing?
components.use: Two to six counters that describe one population (a status funnel, accepted/edited/rejected, failures by stage). Replaces a sentence of counts. Port of the template's Application Status.

components.name: TrendSparkline
components.props: label, data[], plotType?, formatValue?, caption?, tone?
components.use: A SERIES the payload already carries: value + change against the previous point + the curve. Never synthesize a series to decorate. Port of the template's stat-with-sparkline. The text is the accessible reading (the change is spelled out for screen readers) and the drawing is hidden from assistive technology; only the triangle carries the hue, because accent tones fail contrast as small text.

components.name: StatTile
components.props: href | onClick+pressed | neither (plain readout), icon, tone, label, value, hint?
components.use: A counter as a tile: tinted icon band (h-[4.5rem]) + label + value in h5, four across. `href` makes it a link; `onClick`+`pressed` make it a real filter button with aria-pressed. Port of dashboard-analytics-stats. A filter row is THIS, never a hand-written Box.

components.name: QuickActionTile
components.props: href, icon, tone, title, description?
components.use: A shortcut: full-height tinted icon column (w-16) + title. Four across, never two columns. A tile is its icon and its name (the owner, 2026-11-09): a line under it only when it says a state (the month's leader and its votes), never one that repeats the name in other words.

components.name: ModuleTile
components.props: href, icon, trail|null, name, summary, trailLabel?, meta?, status?{kind:'free'|'locked'|'soon',label}
components.use: One tool of the catalog in a grid: the tinted 72px box of StatTile (hue from the trail, TRAIL_TONE) over name, two-line summary and a status line. Every status is a StatusChip: the entry version an account with no purchase installs (entry, positive, with the newest version in meta), outside the plan (neutral), and an app the roadmap has planned (soon, "Em breve", the tile linked to its idea on the roadmap). Use for any grid of modules, in the catalog or inside a recipe.

components.name: UpsellCard
components.props: offer, origin, tone?, title, reason, features[{label,soon?}], soonLabel?, priceLabel, ctaLabel, href
components.use: A rung of the ladder offered without a click, when decideOffers (lib/upsell.ts) says so: both rungs to an account that bought nothing, FlyeeClub Pro to a FlyeeClub member whose use earned it or who is revalidating. States WHY it is here, what the rung adds (a line whose area has nothing published says "Em breve", offerLines in lib/member/offer-copy.ts) and the real price; never a countdown. Records upsell.viewed/upsell.clicked.

components.name: UpgradePrompt
components.props: useUpgradePrompt() -> (feature: ProFeature) => void; UpgradePromptProvider mounted once in components/layout/dashboard-chrome.tsx
components.use: FlyeeClub Pro offered on the click of one of its features (docs/PRODUCT.md, 2026-10-08), never by greying a control out: the control stays enabled and, without the right, calls useUpgradePrompt()(feature) with a feature of lib/upgrade.ts (PRO_FEATURES). The dialog names the feature, lists what Pro adds to the account (proAdditions, the labels of the plans grid, "Em breve" on an empty area), shows the monthly and yearly price from plans and leads to /assinatura?plan=; an account that bought nothing also sees FlyeeClub as the smaller step. The server still refuses the action itself. Records upsell.viewed and upsell.clicked with the feature. A control of an area with nothing published shows "Em breve" instead and opens nothing.

components.name: GuidePanel
components.props: tabs[{depth, guide:{markdown|null, otherLanguage}|null, video:{id,title,durationLabel,youtubeId,completed}|null, soon?}], versionLine, newerLine, upgradeHref
components.use: An app's written guide (usar / abrir o capô) in tabs, from the package of the version shown (migration 0030), with the depth's short video above it. The video loads from youtube-nocookie only on play (lesson.started); the basic depth closed to the plan shows why and links to upgradeHref; the advanced one opens the upgrade prompt; a depth with nothing yet, and an app without any guide, say "Em breve".

components.name: CatalogIcon
components.props: name, size?, className?
components.use: An icon stored by NAME in the database (catalog_modules.icon, catalog_trails.icon). Falls back to the catalog glyph when the icon set lacks the name, so an operator's typo never renders as nothing.

components.name: TILE_TONE
components.props: TILE_TONE[tone] -> { bg, text }
components.use: The only source of icon-container tinting. Never hand-write bg-primary/10 — the template tint is bg-{tone}-light/10.

components.name: ConfirmActionDialog
components.props: title, intro?, consequences[], stays?, staysTitle?, reasonLabel?, reasonPlaceholder?, reasonHelp?, reasonMinLength?, confirmLabel, tone?, onConfirm(reason)->Promise<string|null>, onClose
components.use: Any operator action that changes someone else's account. It forces the three things a confirmation owes the reader: what the action DOES (`consequences`), what it deliberately does NOT do (`stays` — half the risk is assuming it reaches further), and a stated reason for the audit trail. Mount it conditionally with a `key` so it never changes identity on the way out. Never ship a destructive action on a bare click.

components.name: InfoHint
components.props: label, placement?, className?
components.use: What a title, a number or a chip is, behind an "i" a person opens when they want (a bare Tooltip on a non-focusable Box disappears on touch and for keyboards; this is a real button). 200 characters at most, kept by lib/i18n/hint-budget.test.ts. PageHeader and SectionTitle draw it themselves from their `description`; a card head (CardTitle is still a template) puts it beside its own title, with placement="bottom-start" and className="self-center". Never for what must be read before acting (a consequence, a legal note, personal data, values that become public, the instructions a layperson needs on a page of their own): that stays in sight.

components.name: StatusChip
components.props: label, tone? (neutral | primary | positive | attention | info | danger), className?
components.use: A lifecycle state as a NAMED badge: a module version (rascunho, publicada, retirada), a meeting, a roadmap item, a subscription, a lead. The template's tiny pastel button rendered as a span (no focus, reads as text). The tone tints the badge and the word is always text-primary, because the pastel label in the tone itself fails contrast on this palette. Never colour alone, never an outlined Chip for a state.

components.name: ComparisonTable
components.props: caption, rowHeader, columns[{key,label,note?,highlight?}], rows[{key,label,note?,muted?,cells[{primary,secondary?,mark?}]}], footer?, legend?, className?
components.use: A few rows compared across a few columns where every cell is a figure (a metric per segment and week, the leader of each metric per week, results per segment). A real <table> with a sticky first column and a keyboard-reachable horizontal scroll. A `muted` row is set in the secondary text colour, never faded with opacity. Not for managing many rows: that is DataTable.

components.name: AskAiBlock
components.props: label, prompt, copyLabel, copiedLabel, referenceLabel?, command?, className?
components.use: The sentence a member gives their AI (install flyee, add an app, update, reconnect), on the primary tint with a copy button, and the command the AI will run below it as a reference. The member never uses the terminal (docs/PRODUCT.md, 2026-10-08): never show a command as a task, never a terminal block to copy from. The commands live in lib/install-links.ts (REFERENCE_COMMAND) and every sentence (the ask-ai-* keys) ends with installGuideUrl(locale), the address of /instalar.md in the member's language, so the AI finds the commands whether or not flyee is already in the project.

components.name: InstallPathBlock
components.props: locale, cloudHosts: string[] (lib/cli/settings.ts, cloudHostsNow)
components.use: How a member installs flyee (the home and the onboarding install step): first WHERE their AI runs, on the computer in an app, in a terminal, or in a Claude Code session in the cloud, as three choice tiles (a radio group); then the three steps of that path only. The computer and terminal paths keep the AskAiBlock sentence as their second step; the cloud path has the one network change on Claude's screen (its Portuguese labels), the hosts to copy, the button to claude.ai/code with the request written and no environment (cloudSessionUrl), and the login by code. The last answer is remembered in localStorage, a per-viewer convenience. Never sends anyone to a terminal: "No terminal" names where the AI runs.

components.name: DataTable
components.props: rows, columns, loading, header?, actions?, filters?, noRowsOverlay, noResultsOverlay, onQuickFilterChange?, initialColumnVisibility?, enableExport?
components.use: The app's ONE table, and only when the job really is scan/compare/manage many rows. Put the page title in `header` and the primary action in `actions` — those slots render empty otherwise. Imports the community DataGrid, and MUI X stays on its free packages: what only Pro or Premium has (pinned columns, row grouping) is built in our own code, never by switching the wrapper to a paid grid.

components.name: OnboardingChecklist / ActivationProgress / SetupWizard
components.props: see each file
components.use: Steps to first value, completion drive, and progressive disclosure for long setups. Never points, badges, leaderboards or streaks.

components.name: StepCelebrationDialog
components.props: open, title, accomplished, nextTitle, nextHint?, ctaLabel, onNext, onClose
components.use: The beat BETWEEN two steps of a guided flow: names what now exists in her records and loads the next step. Competence feedback, never a token — it awards, counts and ranks nothing, so it stays on the right side of the no-points/badges/leaderboards/streaks rule. Its primary action is what advances the wizard (drive SetupWizard in controlled mode).

template.name: Medidor circular (gauge)
template.props: CircularProgress variant="determinate" + centred label + outline-grey-100 track ring
template.use: One ratio that must read at a glance next to its x/y. No chart library. Not packaged yet — port it when a screen needs a single prominent ratio.

template.name: Tile horizontal com variação
template.props: Card flex-row p-1 + Box h-24 w-16 rounded-2xl bg-{tone}-light/10 + label body1 + value h5 + NiTriangleUp/Down change
template.use: A counter that has a previous period to compare against. Requires real prior-period data — otherwise use StatTile.

template.name: Rosca / radar
template.use: Only above ~6 categories, or to compare two comparable series. Below that, MetricBars reads better — prefer it.

template.name: Card ilustrado
template.props: h4 card-title + body1 + Illustration* h-64 max-w-xs + contained/outlined actions
template.use: The zero-data state of a whole screen, when the path to value deserves more than an EmptyState. Recover the shape with `git show ab2e84d:apps/web/src/components/product/home-empty-banner.tsx`.

template.name: Timeline de atividade
template.props: @mui/lab Timeline + TimelineDot variant=outlined + subtitle2/body2 + relative time
template.use: 'What happened recently' when the order IS the meaning. Recover the shape from the recent-records card in `git show "ab2e84d:apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/inicio/page.tsx"`.

template.name: CardTitle (cabeça de card)
template.props: id, icon, tone? (TileTone), title, description? (behind the i), detail? (a line in sight), chip? (a StatusChip), actions? (QuickActions), as? (h2 | h3)
template.use: The head of a card a person works through: the icon of what the card is on its family's TILE_TONE tint, the title, and on the right where the card stands (a StatusChip) and what it keeps one click away (QuickActions). What the card is for goes behind the "i" beside the title (`description`, about 200 characters at most), never a paragraph under it; `detail` is the one line in sight, only for state or data that tells the card apart (how many a list shows) or for what must be read before acting (a consequence). Until it is built, a card puts an InfoHint beside its own title. A person tells the cards apart, and sees which one asks for something, before reading any of them. A card that leads with a bare heading reads like every other card. Packaged in the ONE project (C:\AppsProjects\one, built on this same template): port it from its apps/web/src/components/product/card-title.tsx.

template.name: StateLine (linha de estado)
template.props: tone (done | waiting | attention | failed | info), children, status?, action?, icon?, emphasis?
template.use: Where ONE thing stands, in a sentence, with an icon in the colour of its state: done (success, a check), waiting (the warning hue, a clock: under way, nobody needs to act; never the primary yellow), attention (accent-3, an exclamation: a person should look or act), failed (error, kept for a failure), info (grey, only said). The words keep the text colours, so the state reads from them too. `status` is the state in its own words at the end of the line, so the states of a list line up on the right and stay on the line on a phone; `action` is the one thing the line still asks for, beside it; `emphasis` boxes the line on its tint when it is the card's answer ('Nada mais a enviar'). Things listed with their states are StateLines, never plain sentences. Packaged in the ONE project (C:\AppsProjects\one, built on this same template): port it from its apps/web/src/components/product/state-line.tsx.

template.name: QuickActions (ações de um clique)
template.props: label, actions[{key, label, icon?, onClick, disabled?}], icon?, text?, align? (left | right)
template.use: What a card keeps out of sight, one click away: a request already fulfilled that may be made again (another copy, a new link), or what a person seldom needs. An icon button with its name on hover (with `text`, words beside the icon) opening a menu, each action with its icon. What the card asks for now stays a button of its own, in view, on the line it is about: never hide in here the only way to do the card's pending job, nor a right the person must find in plain sight (withdrawing a consent, deleting their data), nor a Pro feature, which is offered on its own click (UpgradePrompt). Packaged in the ONE project (C:\AppsProjects\one, built on this same template): port it from its apps/web/src/components/product/quick-actions.tsx.

template.name: OutcomeDialog (desfecho de um ato)
template.props: open, tone? (done | info), title, lines[{key, icon, text}], closeLabel, onClose
template.use: What an act a person just did changed, said whole and in front of them: an answer that binds them (a consent given or taken back), a decision others will act on. A large icon on its tint, the title in the person's words, one consequence a line with its icon, and one button ('Entendi'). An Alert or a toast at the top of the page is read past: an act whose consequences the person must understand is confirmed here. Not for the routine save of a form (the field's own state says it) nor for the beat between setup steps (StepCelebrationDialog). Packaged in the ONE project (C:\AppsProjects\one, built on this same template): port it from its apps/web/src/components/product/outcome-dialog.tsx.

template.name: ProgressSteps / ProgressNow / ProgressBar / ProgressCounts / ProgressList (andamento)
template.props: ProgressSteps(steps[{key,label,state: done|current|next|stopped,when?,icon}], label, stateWords, working?, href?) · ProgressNow(tone: progress|done|stopped, lead, text, extra?, action?, working?) · ProgressBar(steps, reached, state: progress|done|stopped, label) · ProgressCounts(steps[{key,label,icon,count,href,countLabel}], label) · ProgressList(rows[{key,href,title,detail?,step,steps,reached,state,label}], label)
template.use: Where something stands along its way. ProgressSteps draws its steps in order, each with its icon: done (primary tint), under way (the warning hue, never red), still to come (outline), with the day each began, across from md and one under the other on a phone; the step under way turns only while the product works there now (`working`, default true), and a step may link to the card where it is done (`href`). ProgressNow says under it, in a sentence, what happens now and who it is with, with the one action the reader may take, and shows a clock in place of the spinner while the way waits for somebody (`working={false}`). ProgressBar is the same way in small for a row of a list; ProgressCounts shows how many things are at each step, each step a link to its list; ProgressList is the latest few things along their way, one line each with the step in words and its ProgressBar, each a link to it, for a home where the whole list is one click further. A timeline tells every event; this tells the few that mark the way. Packaged in the ONE project (C:\AppsProjects\one, built on this same template): port it from its apps/web/src/components/product/progress-steps.tsx.

traps: MUI 9 builds a component class list as `Mui{Comp}-{variant}` + `Mui{Comp}-color{Color}`; the composed `Mui{Comp}-{variant}{Color}` of MUI 5 is gone. Both known instances are fixed: style/inputs/button.css now targets `.MuiButton-pastel.MuiButton-color{Color}`, and style/data-display/chip.css now targets `.MuiChip-outlined.MuiChip-color{Color}`. An outlined Chip therefore paints BOTH its text (from MUI emotion, matched on props) and its 1px ring (from the template, matched on classes). Before writing a selector against a composed class, check useUtilityClasses in the installed component source — TypeScript will not catch it, because a ChipClasses/ButtonClasses augmentation can declare a class the DOM never receives.
useHighlightedSparkline derives its y-axis from the data: an empty array yields -Infinity. Guard the series before rendering.
The template's `caption` variant is below 12px. Consequence text ('this is recorded with your name') belongs in body2.

An outlined Chip ring inherits the raw colour token, so it is only as legible as that token: on the light theme, error/primary/accent-* clear the 3:1 floor for a graphical object, while info (2.12:1), success (2.13:1), warning (2.51:1) and secondary (2.77:1) do not. Use colour on a Chip as reinforcement of a word that is already in the label, never as the sole carrier of the state.

A colour prop that is CONSTANT down a whole column carries no information and costs contrast: it reads as an affordance (primary) or dilutes the one signal that matters (error). Colour a Chip only where the colour VARIES with the row.

Feedback severity tokens (`--{sev}-light` / `--{sev}-dark`) hold the SAME value in the light and the dark block of design-tokens/css/common.css. A rule written as `text-{sev}-dark` for the light theme is therefore automatically wrong in the dark one, and no `dark:` variant exists to save it. Measured on the Alert: the template pairing of `bg-{sev}-light/10` + `text-{sev}-dark` reads 2.51:1 (info), 2.56:1 (success), 2.95:1 (warning) on light and 2.15:1 for error on dark, against ~9.2:1 for the inherited text. Severity belongs in the BACKGROUND and the ICON; the words keep inheriting text-primary.

The palette is written as `hsl(var(--token))` with cssVariables on. decomposeColor cannot read that and returns NaN WITHOUT throwing, so MUI never reaches its own fallback: every DERIVED colour (theme.alpha, palette.Alert.{sev}StandardBg, getContrastText) resolves to a value the browser discards. Direct references such as palette[sev].main survive — which is why an Alert icon is coloured today while its background is not. Consequence: when a template selector dies there is no native styling underneath it, and any new component that leans on a computed MUI colour is born broken and silent.

Run `npm run check:mui-classes` after touching anything under apps/web/src/style/**. It matches every `.Mui{Comp}-{slot}` against that component's own class manifest in node_modules, the only source of truth: a ChipClasses/ButtonClasses type augmentation can declare a class the DOM never emits, and that is exactly how three stylesheets accumulated dead rules nobody could see.

COLOUR ON A LABEL, MEASURED. This theme's palette is too light on six of its ten colours to carry text, and neither MUI nor the template compensates. Light theme, against the 4.5:1 floor: a FILLED surface (contained Button, filled Chip, Fab, selected ToggleButton) paints the label with `contrastText` = white, which clears only primary 4.89, accent-2 4.51, accent-4 5.22 and error 5.31 — it fails secondary 2.77, accent-1 3.77, accent-3 3.55, info 2.12, warning 2.51, success 2.13. An OUTLINED Chip does NOT rescue it: MUI paints that label `palette[color].main`, the same tone, so outlined warning is also 2.51. The pastel badge is no better (warning 2.95). Only three ways out, in order of preference: fill with one of the four colours that pass; or keep the tone in the RING and give the label `text-text-primary!` (9.79:1), which is what the alert chips of the inherited clinical-context-bar.tsx did (git show ab2e84d:apps/web/src/components/product/clinical-context-bar.tsx); or state the severity in the word and drop the colour. Never assume a variant change fixes contrast — measure it.
